  have hne : ∀ i, (1 : ℂ) - a i * (p i : ℂ) ^ (-s) ≠ 0 := fun i => sub_ne_zero.mpr (Ne.symm (h i))
  have hdsub : ∀ i, DifferentiableAt ℂ (fun s : ℂ => 1 - a i * (p i : ℂ) ^ (-s)) s :=
    fun i => (hasDerivAt_one_sub_param (hp i) (a i) s).differentiableAt
  have hd : ∀ i, DifferentiableAt ℂ (fun s : ℂ => (1 - a i * (p i : ℂ) ^ (-s))⁻¹) s :=

    logDeriv_prod (fun i _ => inv_ne_zero (hne i)) (fun i _ => hd i)

    intro i
    have hinv : (fun s : ℂ => (1 - a i * (p i : ℂ) ^ (-s))⁻¹)
        = fun s : ℂ => 1 / (1 - a i * (p i : ℂ) ^ (-s)) := by
      funext t; rw [one_div]
    rw [hinv, logDeriv_div s one_ne_zero (hne i) (differentiableAt_const 1) (hdsub i),
      logDeriv_const]
    simp only [Pi.zero_apply, zero_sub]
    rw [logDeriv_apply, (hasDerivAt_one_sub_param (hp i) (a i) s).deriv]
  rw [hL]
  simp only [hterm, Finset.sum_neg_distrib, neg_neg]
  exact eulerFlux_eq p a s

## Theorem

The direct reciprocal symmetrization of a positive local Euler weight `a` produces

```text
(1+a z)(1+a^(-1)z)
  = 1 + (a+a^(-1))z + z^2.
```

Its normalized two-spin coefficient is

```text
c(a) = (a+a^(-1))/2.
```

Lean proves, for `a>0`,

```text
c(a) >= 1,
leeYangPairCircle(c(a)) <-> a=1.
```

Therefore every genuine contracting Euler weight `0<a<1` yields a reciprocal quadratic with an
off-circle pair.  For example `a=1/2` gives roots `-1/2` and `-2`.

Reciprocal field pairing is exactly the wrong operation.  A finite Ising detour must place the
arithmetic data in ferromagnetic interaction weights

```text

```

not in a local fugacity and its inverse.  The completed prime--Gamma source must therefore build
nonnegative couplings or a verified Lee--Yang single-site measure.  Functional-equation pairing of
Euler factors does not provide the finite circle theorem.

## Universal law

Heat depth and Euler Fisher order are two coordinates on one prime-power moment carrier. Define the
mixed moment by multiplying the heat base measure by the `k`th reciprocal-prime-power node and the
`m`th logarithmic-energy power. It is exactly the `m`th Euler Fisher moment at inverse temperature
`1 - sigma + q + k`. Therefore, for every logarithmic order `m`,

```text
2^(1-sigma+q+k) * mixedMoment(sigma,q,k,m) -> (log 2)^m.
```

The `m=0` member is the raw real heat-aperture log echo, giving its exact dyadic normalization and
prime-two ground-state limit `1`. The `m=2` member is the shifted Fisher conformal scale.

For each prime-power node `N`, multiplication by its `k`th reciprocal power changes
`N^(-(1-sigma+q))` into `N^(-(1-sigma+q+k))`; the logarithmic-energy power is untouched. Termwise
equality gives the mixed/Fisher identity. Compose the all-real inverse-temperature ground-selection
theorem with the cofinal map `k |-> 1-sigma+q+k`. At logarithmic order zero, the heat-echo moment
identity removes the energy factor and identifies the mixed sum with the raw echo.

# Gamma--prime hybrid Euler--Weierstrass--Fredholm universality law

Status: Stage 2 — dependency-closed paper proof; Lean exact check passed

## Theorem-generated discovery

`HTGeometry.GammaWeierstrass` realizes the reciprocal Gamma Weierstrass factor as a regularized
Fredholm determinant of the diagonal `-s/(n+1)`. `RHTower.FredholmDeterminantZeta` realizes
`zeta(s)⁻¹` as the trace-class determinant of the prime diagonal `p⁻ˢ`. The corpus explicitly
calls these archimedean and Euler analogues, but supplies no operator on their disjoint carrier.

`GammaXiHybridWeierstrassFredholmUniversalityLaw` supplies reusable sum-type operator geometry for
the different pairing of the Gamma branch with the Xi divisor. Replacing the Xi block by the Euler
prime block produces a distinct determinant and an unconditional real spectral phase.

## Statement

For every real `sigma > 1`, put on `ℕ ⊕ Nat.Primes` the diagonal spectrum

`n ↦ -sigma/(n+1)` and `p ↦ p^(-sigma)`.

The resulting operator:

1. is Hilbert--Schmidt and compact;
2. is injective;
3. has the natural-number basis as an approximate unit kernel, hence has nonclosed range;
4. is self-adjoint;
5. has regularized determinant at `1`

   `det₂(1-T) =
     (sigma exp(gamma sigma) Gamma(sigma))⁻¹
     zeta(sigma)⁻¹ exp(P(sigma))`,

   where `P(sigma) = sum_p p^(-sigma)` is the convergent prime trace.

Equivalently, removing the prime trace correction from the one hybrid determinant gives exactly
the product of the reciprocal archimedean Gamma factor and reciprocal Euler zeta factor.

## Dependency-closed proof

The reciprocal-integer Gamma branch is square summable. For `sigma > 1`, the prime branch is
absolutely summable and therefore square summable. Sum-type summability makes the hybrid diagonal
Hilbert--Schmidt, hence compact. Every coordinate is nonzero. Coordinate evaluation therefore
proves injectivity. The Gamma branch tends to zero and supplies unit coordinate vectors whose
images tend to zero; the existing approximate-kernel criterion converts injectivity into
nonclosed range.

All Gamma entries are real and all positive-prime real powers are positive real, so the diagonal
kernel equals its Hilbert--Schmidt adjoint.

The diagonal determinant product splits across the sum type. The natural-number product is the
existing Gamma Weierstrass factor. The prime product splits into the bare Euler product
`zeta(sigma)⁻¹` and the exponential of its absolutely convergent trace. Multiplying gives the
identity.

No computation, numerical approximation, RH premise, or new analytic axiom is used.

# Framed relative completion index

## Big picture

`ULF-FBG-002` constructs source formation as a framed nuclear cycle. Its multiplier projection
has a fixed norm-one defect at every nonzero grade, while its prime-mixed nuclear shadow is a
trace-norm loop of trace one. This proves why unframed completion is information-neutral and why
every closed scalar reader loses the grade.

The next object is not another producer, receiver, or projection. It is the **relative class of
two reciprocal framed completions after their common four-channel `J`-frame is removed**.

Fresh comparison retired the naive version of this programme. Theta normal formation depends on
`delta log p`, while cubic completion depends on `(log p)/delta`; they do not have the same
one-dimensional principal symbol. `ULF-FBG-005` proves the correct gluing: the two variables are
reciprocal legs with product `(log p)^2`, and their compact/split tensor has an exact `O(2,2)`
`J`-Gram equal to the full prime-mixed `T`.

## Required theorem

Construct from literal integer/Poisson formation, before divisor specialization,

```text
mathfrak T_E      Euler/prime reciprocal framed nuclear cycle,
mathfrak T_theta  additive theta-completion reciprocal framed cycle,
K_univ            their common four-channel J-principal frame.              (FRC.1)
```

Prove all of the following as one theorem:

1. both cycles factor through `K_univ`, with theta and completion occupying its reciprocal legs;
2. subtracting `K_univ` gives a canonical relative mapping-cone class `Delta_rel`;
3. `Delta_rel` retains prime/depth labels and unsquared Euler coefficients;
4. it has a source-derived nuclear representative `R_rel` satisfying

```text
||R_rel||_1 <= B_Euler < 1;                                      (FRC.2)
```

5. completion pairs `Delta_rel` with the unsigned horizon cocycle, and after specialization

```text
<Delta_rel,horizon_q> = thetaKakutaniEscapeMultiplicity(q) in Z. (FRC.3)
```

Then any strict-right copy would give an integer equal to one by the existing escape theorem but
strictly below one by `(FRC.2)`, contradiction. Reflection excludes strict-left copies.

## First attack: completion functor on the reciprocal `J`-Gram

The Route-P identity already proves primewise

```text
formation metric anomaly
 = phase-matched completion companion + primitive source weight.             (FRC.4)
```

Both metric terms are nonsummable; their difference is the summable unsquared primitive source.
`ULF-FBG-001/002` supplies degree-one projective normal frame, exact normal/cotangent
transgression, and norm-one prime-infinity projection jump. `ULF-FBG-005` supplies its reciprocal
split completion frame and proves on every finite packet

```text
A_(delta,E)* J A_(delta,E)=T_E.                                  (FRC.5)
```

First unresolved theorem is functoriality of `(FRC.5)` under the actual singular theta
completion. It must preserve the `J`-Gram cancellation before positive closure, absolute value,
or observer trace, while its relative remainder inherits a native Schatten-one bound. Equality

/-!
# The Möbius contraction carries the reciprocal squarefree Euler transfer

The actual normalized all-prime Möbius shift has Laplace multiplier

`ζ(2σ) / (ζ(σ) ζ(σ + πx))`.

The higher-trace squarefree correction `ζ(2(σ+πx))/ζ(2σ)` is holomorphic and nonzero on the
Euler half-plane.  Their product is exactly the reciprocal squarefree Euler factor, with only the
base normalization `ζ(σ)⁻¹` left over.  Thus the first-trace reciprocal transfer is already the
characteristic multiplier of the source Möbius contraction, not a divisor-defined response.
-/

open Complex

noncomputable section

namespace RHTower

/-- The harmless higher-trace correction from the Möbius multiplier to the reciprocal
squarefree Euler multiplier. -/
def mobiusSquarefreeSafeCorrection (sigma x : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  riemannZeta (2 * (((sigma + Real.pi * x : ℝ) : ℂ))) /
    riemannZeta (2 * (sigma : ℂ))

/-- The source-defined reciprocal squarefree transfer. -/
def mobiusSquarefreeReciprocalTransfer (sigma x : ℝ) : ℂ :=
  mobiusSquarefreeSafeCorrection sigma x * infiniteMobiusLaplaceMultiplier sigma x

/-- The safe correction cancels the fixed second-trace normalization and leaves exactly the
reciprocal squarefree Euler factor, normalized at the base by `ζ(σ)⁻¹`. -/
theorem mobiusSquarefreeReciprocalTransfer_eq
    {sigma x : ℝ} (hsigma : 1 < sigma) (hx : 0 ≤ x) :
    mobiusSquarefreeReciprocalTransfer sigma x =
      riemannZeta (2 * (((sigma + Real.pi * x : ℝ) : ℂ))) /
        (riemannZeta (sigma : ℂ) *
          riemannZeta (((sigma + Real.pi * x : ℝ) : ℂ))) := by
  have htwoSigma : riemannZeta (2 * (sigma : ℂ)) ≠ 0 :=
    riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re (by
      simp
      linarith)
  rw [mobiusSquarefreeReciprocalTransfer, mobiusSquarefreeSafeCorrection,
    infiniteMobiusLaplaceMultiplier_eq_zetaRatio hsigma hx]
  field_simp [htwoSigma]

/-- Multiplying back the base residue normalization recovers the literal reciprocal squarefree
Euler quotient `ζ(2s)/ζ(s)`. -/
theorem riemannZeta_mul_mobiusSquarefreeReciprocalTransfer_eq
    {sigma x : ℝ} (hsigma : 1 < sigma) (hx : 0 ≤ x) :
    riemannZeta (sigma : ℂ) * mobiusSquarefreeReciprocalTransfer sigma x =
      riemannZeta (2 * (((sigma + Real.pi * x : ℝ) : ℂ))) /
        riemannZeta (((sigma + Real.pi * x : ℝ) : ℂ)) := by
  have hsigmaZeta : riemannZeta (sigma : ℂ) ≠ 0 :=
    riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re (by simpa using hsigma)
  have hshiftZeta :
      riemannZeta (((sigma + Real.pi * x : ℝ) : ℂ)) ≠ 0 :=
    riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re (by
      simp
      nlinarith [Real.pi_pos])
  rw [mobiusSquarefreeReciprocalTransfer_eq hsigma hx]
  field_simp [hsigmaZeta, hshiftZeta]

end RHTower

/-!
# Finite Euler factors as reciprocal Gamma pairs

Euler's reflection formula gives an unconditional reciprocal-Gamma expression
for every finite Euler factor.  The formulation uses inverses of Gamma values,
so it remains valid at the apparent Gamma-pole locations.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace GaloisForLFunctions.RHTower

open Complex

/-- The imaginary Gamma slope associated with a finite prime. -/
def finiteEulerGammaSlope (p : Nat.Primes) : ℂ :=
  Complex.I * (Real.log p : ℂ) / (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ))

/-- The Euler--Gamma slope has no real component. -/
theorem finiteEulerGammaSlope_re (p : Nat.Primes) :
    (finiteEulerGammaSlope p).re = 0 := by
  set L : ℝ := Real.log (p : ℝ)
  change (Complex.I * (L : ℂ) / (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ))).re = 0
  simp [Complex.div_re]

/-- Every prime produces a genuinely upper-imaginary Gamma slope. -/
theorem finiteEulerGammaSlope_im_pos (p : Nat.Primes) :
    0 < (finiteEulerGammaSlope p).im := by
  set L : ℝ := Real.log (p : ℝ)
  have hlog : 0 < Real.log ((p : ℕ) : ℝ) :=
    Real.log_pos (by exact_mod_cast p.property.one_lt)
  change 0 < (Complex.I * (L : ℂ) / (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ))).im
  have hL : 0 < L := hlog
  simp [Complex.div_im, hL, Real.pi_pos]

/-- The reciprocal Gamma pair associated with one finite Euler factor. -/
def finiteEulerGammaReciprocalPair (p : Nat.Primes) (s : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  (Complex.Gamma (finiteEulerGammaSlope p * s) *
    Complex.Gamma (1 - finiteEulerGammaSlope p * s))⁻¹

/-- The finite semilocal inverse Euler multiplier. -/
def finiteEulerSemilocalProduct (S : Finset Nat.Primes) (s : ℂ) : ℂ :=
  ∏ p ∈ S, finiteEulerLocalFactor p s

/-- **Finite Euler--Gamma reflection weld.**  Every prime Euler factor is exactly a reciprocal
Gamma pair with its canonical imaginary slope. -/
theorem finiteEulerLocalFactor_eq_reciprocalGammaPair (p : Nat.Primes) (s : ℂ) :
    finiteEulerLocalFactor p s =
      -2 * Complex.I * (Real.pi : ℂ) *
        Complex.exp (-((Real.log p : ℂ) * s) / 2) *
        (Complex.Gamma (finiteEulerGammaSlope p * s) *
          Complex.Gamma (1 - finiteEulerGammaSlope p * s))⁻¹ := by
  let u : ℂ := Complex.I * (Real.log p : ℂ) * s / (2 * (Real.pi : ℂ))
  let x : ℂ := (Real.log p : ℂ) * s
  have hpi : (Real.pi : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr Real.pi_ne_zero
  have hrecip : (Complex.Gamma u * Complex.Gamma (1 - u))⁻¹ =
      Complex.sin ((Real.pi : ℂ) * u) / (Real.pi : ℂ) := by
    rw [Complex.Gamma_mul_Gamma_one_sub, inv_div]
  have hsin : Complex.sin ((Real.pi : ℂ) * u) =
      Complex.I / 2 * (Complex.exp (x / 2) - Complex.exp (-(x / 2))) := by
    rw [show (Real.pi : ℂ) * u = (x / 2) * Complex.I by
      dsimp [u, x]
      field_simp [hpi]]
    rw [Complex.sin_mul_I]
    unfold Complex.sinh
    ring
  have hsum : Complex.exp (-(x / 2)) * Complex.exp (x / 2) = 1 := by
    rw [← Complex.exp_add]
    have : -(x / 2) + x / 2 = 0 := by ring
    rw [this, Complex.exp_zero]
  have hsq : Complex.exp (-(x / 2)) * Complex.exp (-(x / 2)) = Complex.exp (-x) := by
    rw [← Complex.exp_add]
    congr 1
    ring
  unfold finiteEulerLocalFactor
  rw [show -s * (Real.log p : ℂ) = -x by
    dsimp [x]
    ring]
  rw [show finiteEulerGammaSlope p * s = u by
    dsimp [finiteEulerGammaSlope, u]
    ring,
    show (Real.log p : ℂ) * s = x by rfl, hrecip, hsin]
  field_simp [hpi]
  rw [Complex.I_sq]
  calc
    1 - Complex.exp (-x) =
        Complex.exp (-(x / 2)) * Complex.exp (x / 2) -
          Complex.exp (-(x / 2)) * Complex.exp (-(x / 2)) := by rw [hsum, hsq]
    _ = Complex.exp (-(x / 2)) *
          (Complex.exp (x / 2) - Complex.exp (-(x / 2))) := by ring
    _ = -(-1 * (Complex.exp (-(x / 2)) *
          (Complex.exp (x / 2) - Complex.exp (-(x / 2))))) := by ring
    _ = -(-1 * Complex.exp (-(x / 2)) *
          (Complex.exp (x / 2) - Complex.exp (-(x / 2)))) := by ring

/-- The local Euler--Gamma weld in terms of the named reciprocal Gamma pair. -/
theorem finiteEulerLocalFactor_eq_gammaReciprocalPair (p : Nat.Primes) (s : ℂ) :
    finiteEulerLocalFactor p s =
      -2 * Complex.I * (Real.pi : ℂ) *
        Complex.exp (-((Real.log p : ℂ) * s) / 2) *
        finiteEulerGammaReciprocalPair p s := by
  simpa only [finiteEulerGammaReciprocalPair] using
    finiteEulerLocalFactor_eq_reciprocalGammaPair p s

/-- The functional-equation-symmetric Euler quartet is a four-factor reciprocal-Gamma
weld with a constant exponential gauge. -/
theorem finiteEulerLocalQuartet_eq_gammaReciprocalQuartet
    (p : Nat.Primes) (s : ℂ) :
    finiteEulerLocalQuartet p s =
      (-2 * Complex.I * (Real.pi : ℂ)) ^ 2 *
        Complex.exp (-((Real.log p : ℂ) / 2)) *
        (finiteEulerGammaReciprocalPair p s *
          finiteEulerGammaReciprocalPair p (1 - s)) := by
  rw [finiteEulerLocalQuartet,
    finiteEulerLocalFactor_eq_gammaReciprocalPair p s,
    finiteEulerLocalFactor_eq_gammaReciprocalPair p (1 - s)]

/-!
# Canonical normalization of the theta-source divisor mode

At a zero of the completed theta-source transform, the explicit two-ended mode
`u_z = sourceModeU thetaSource z` decays exponentially.  This closes the two analytic hypotheses
previously left on the divisor-to-eigenvector map:

* `f_z = -z u_z` is integrable;
* its total integral is exactly the source mass.

Indeed `u_z' = D_z`, `f_z = -i D_z + k`, and the two endpoint values of `u_z` vanish, so the
whole-line fundamental theorem of calculus gives `∫ D_z = 0` and hence `∫ f_z = ∫ k = M`.
Consequently every theta-source divisor in the strip produces a genuine eigenfunction of the
source inverse, with no assumed endpoint normalization or integrability data.
-/

open MeasureTheory Set Filter Topology

namespace RHTower

noncomputable section

open GaloisForLFunctions.HTGeometry

/-- The source-pointed mode at a theta-source zero is Lebesgue integrable. -/
theorem integrable_sourceModeU_thetaSource {z : ℂ} (hz : |z.im| < 1)
    (hzero : xiC thetaSource z = 0) :
    Integrable (sourceModeU thetaSource z) (volume : Measure ℝ) :=
  integrable_sourceModeU hz hzero

/-- The right mode `f_z = -z u_z` at a theta-source zero is Lebesgue integrable. -/
theorem integrable_sourceModeF_thetaSource {z : ℂ} (hz : |z.im| < 1)
    (hzero : xiC thetaSource z = 0) :
    Integrable (sourceModeF thetaSource z) (volume : Measure ℝ) := by
  refine ((integrable_sourceModeU_thetaSource hz hzero).const_mul (-z)).congr ?_
  filter_upwards with x
  rw [sourceModeF]

/-- The theta-source mode vanishes at the left endpoint. -/
theorem tendsto_sourceModeU_thetaSource_atBot {z : ℂ} (hz : |z.im| < 1)
    (hzero : xiC thetaSource z = 0) :
    Tendsto (sourceModeU thetaSource z) atBot (𝓝 0) :=
  tendsto_sourceModeU_atBot hz hzero

/-- The theta-source mode vanishes at the right endpoint. -/
theorem tendsto_sourceModeU_thetaSource_atTop {z : ℂ} (hz : |z.im| < 1)
    (hzero : xiC thetaSource z = 0) :
    Tendsto (sourceModeU thetaSource z) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
  tendsto_sourceModeU_atTop hz hzero

/-- **Canonical source-mode normalization.**  At every theta-source zero in the strip, the right
mode carries exactly the full source mass.  The equality is forced by the two endpoint values and
is not an additional eigenvector hypothesis. -/
theorem integral_sourceModeF_thetaSource_eq_mass {z : ℂ} (hz : |z.im| < 1)
    (hzero : xiC thetaSource z = 0) :
    (∫ x, sourceModeF thetaSource z x) = (thetaSource.mass : ℂ) := by
  have hf := integrable_sourceModeF_thetaSource hz hzero
  have hk : Integrable (fun x : ℝ => (thetaSource.k x : ℂ))
      (volume : Measure ℝ) := thetaSource.integrable_k.ofReal
  have hD : Integrable (sourceModeD thetaSource z) (volume : Measure ℝ) := by
    refine ((hf.sub hk).const_mul Complex.I).congr ?_
    filter_upwards with x
    exact (sourceModeD_eq thetaSource z x).symm
  have hzeroD : (∫ x, sourceModeD thetaSource z x) = 0 := by
    have h := MeasureTheory.integral_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto
      (hasDerivAt_sourceModeU thetaSource (hasShiftedTail_thetaSource hz)) hD
      (tendsto_sourceModeU_thetaSource_atBot hz hzero)
      (tendsto_sourceModeU_thetaSource_atTop hz hzero)
    simpa only [sourceModeD, sub_zero] using h
  calc
